chunks: And from him, from al-Naḍr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the two rakʿahs of fajr: before fajr or after fajr? He said: Before fajr. Indeed, they are part of salat al-layl, making salat al-layl thirteen rakʿahs. Do you wish to make an analogy? If you had something due from the month of Ramadan, would you perform a voluntary act when the time of the obligatory duty had entered? Then begin with the obligatory duty.

key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory religious duty that takes priority
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ: the two rakʿahs associated with fajr prayer
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, mentioned here regarding an owed obligatory fast
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer of the late night worship cycle
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the time when the obligatory act has begun

ai.seo_question: Should the two rakʿahs of fajr be prayed before fajr or after it?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the two rakʿahs of fajr are to be performed before fajr and are counted as part of salat al-layl, totaling thirteen rakʿahs. It also establishes a legal principle that when the time of an obligatory act has entered, the obligatory act takes precedence over voluntary worship.
